about: Keychain dialogs on macOS, the same in both SDKs (the keychain-ux lane, 2026-09-27).

Read by python/tests/skills/local/test_keychain_ux_store.py, python/tests/cli/test_keychain_ux_cli.py, typescript/tests/unit/skills/keychain-ux-store.test.ts and typescript/tests/unit/cli/keychain-ux-cli.test.ts. The real keychain is touched only by python/tests/skills/local/test_keychain_ux_macos_probe.py and typescript/tests/unit/skills/keychain-ux-macos-probe.test.ts, with probe items of their own.

service: the keychain service each SDK files its items under. Each SDK reads only its own, so macOS never asks one SDK about the other's items. legacy_template is the name both SDKs shared before: an SDK that finds none of its own item copies the old one once and leaves it in place.
names: the words for each runtime in sentences. program_name: the name macOS shows in its dialog, from the path of the running program (a bundle's name when it runs inside NAME.app/Contents/MacOS/).
record: the file beside the items that says which program last used each one. It holds no secret. predictions: what a recorded program and the current one mean for the next read.

explanation: the four lines said once per run, in a terminal, before a read that may raise a dialog. blocked: the one sentence a run with nobody to answer says instead of reading. left_behind: what logout and secrets remove say about an old item they cannot remove without a dialog.

no_quiet_read: where a no-dialog read exists. Python proves one (SecKeychainSetUserInteractionAllowed, per process). TypeScript cannot make one: @napi-rs/keyring has no such switch and node has no FFI, so it decides from the record and an attribute-only lookup, and bounds a read with nobody to answer by a timeout.
doctor: the words of the `keychain` line, also the chat's /status `Keychain` row. credentials_file: the profile's account metadata file and its mode.

record.where: Beside the store's secrets folder: in its parent when the folder is called `secrets` (the profile's folder, ~/.webagents or ~/.webagents-<profile>), else inside it as file_elsewhere.
record.about: Which program last used each webagents keychain item on this machine. macOS asks before a different program reads an item, and webagents reads this file to say so first. It holds no secret.

sample.about: Which program last used each webagents keychain item on this machine. macOS asks before a different program reads an item, and webagents reads this file to say so first. It holds no secret.

predictions.about: the same program as last time
an upgrade: a new version at a new path
a reinstall: the same version and path, a different binary
another installation of the same version
no record for an item that exists
a record without a stamp compares path and version

explanation: macOS is about to ask whether {program} may use "{item}" in your keychain: {program} is what webagents runs on.
Choose Always Allow so it does not ask again.
If it asks for your Mac password, the password goes to macOS, never to webagents.
webagents only ever asks for items whose name starts with "webagents", so choose Deny for anything else.
blocked: macOS may ask before {program} can use "{item}" in your keychain, and nothing here can answer it: run `{command}` once in a terminal, then try again.
left_behind: "{item}" ({account}) from an earlier version of webagents is still in your keychain, because removing it would make macOS ask. To remove it, open Keychain Access, search for "{item}" and delete it.
denied: macOS did not allow {program} to use "{item}", so webagents carries on without it.
no_default_keychain: macOS has no default keychain for this user here (HOME is {home}), and making one would raise a dialog

other_runtime.signed_in: The {other} is signed in on this machine, but each CLI keeps its own sign-in in the keychain.
other_runtime.keys: The {other} has keys stored on this machine, but each CLI keeps its own: store them for this one with `{command}`.

no_quiet_read.python: SecKeychainSetUserInteractionAllowed(false) around each keychain call: with nobody to answer, macOS returns an error instead of a dialog (measured 2026-09-27 on macOS 26.2 with probe items /usr/bin/security and node created: errSecAuthFailed -25293 for a read, errSecInvalidOwnerEdit -25244 for a delete).
no_quiet_read.typescript: none: @napi-rs/keyring has no switch for it and node has no FFI. The record and an attribute-only `security find-generic-password` lookup decide whether a read may ask; a read in a run with nobody to answer is bounded by a timeout.

credentials_file.name: credentials.json
credentials_file.about: The profile's account metadata beside the keychain token: username, user id and expiry, never the token. The Python CLI writes it 0600 and repairs a looser mode when it reads it. The TypeScript CLI writes none: its whoami asks the platform, so the test there pins that it never creates one and that the record it does write is 0600.
